issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect StockIngredient to have a constructor with signature StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template's StockIngredient class only provides a constructor with an extra boolean parameter (String, int, int, boolean). This mismatch means code in the template (and examples in the problem) that instantiate StockIngredient with three arguments will not compile against the provided template, confusing students and preventing them from following the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template's StockIngredient class to provide the three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) (either by replacing the current constructor or by adding an overloaded constructor that delegates to existing validation logic). This will align the template with the problem specification and the solution, preventing compile errors and student confusion.

issues.description: Constructor API mismatch for StockIngredient across artifacts: the problem statement and the solution expect a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template's StockIngredient only exposes a four-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean strictValidation). This divergence in parameter list (an extra boolean parameter name 'strictValidation' in the template) breaks the conceptual/API mapping students must follow (Main and SealSaloon usage assume the 3-arg constructor) and may cause confusion and compilation issues.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template API with the problem statement and solution by adding a three-argument constructor to the template StockIngredient class: public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) { this(name, price, quantity, false); } or replace the four-argument constructor with the three-argument version. This preserves existing strict validation logic while matching the expected constructor signature used in Main and SealSaloon.
